verdict: Arista's revenue jumped 58% to $3.66B — its fastest growth since its IPO — as builders of AI data centers bought its networking gear at a record pace.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +58% YoY — the fastest growth since its IPO

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: Slightly below last year's 64.6% on product mix

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Switches and routers for data centers — the hardware AI clusters use to move data between servers. Up 67%.

segments.name: Service
segments.note: Support and service contracts on installed gear — steadier, recurring revenue, up 18%.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next switches and the CloudVision software that runs them.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling to cloud giants and large enterprises.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

otherDetail: Interest income on Arista's cash pile plus gains on strategic investments of $135M, less other items — $273M, net.

takeaways.title: AI spending is Arista's rocket fuel
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 58.5% to $3.66B, beating the company's own $3.3B guidance. Product revenue — the switches and routers that connect AI servers — rose 67%, as cloud and AI customers raced to build out data centers.

takeaways.title: Growth barely dented profitability
takeaways.text: Even while spending to keep up with demand, Arista kept a 63.6% gross margin and turned 44.9 cents of every revenue dollar into operating profit. Net income nearly doubled to $1.56B.

takeaways.title: Investment gains added a bonus
takeaways.text: Other income of $273M included about $135M of gains on strategic investments, on top of interest earned on cash. It is a helpful extra, but the core story is the product business, which produced most of the profit.

oneTimers: Other income includes roughly $135M of gains on strategic investments (paper gains on stakes Arista holds). Arista's non-GAAP results exclude them; non-GAAP operating income was $1,796M.
